description: This walk follows the Nenagh River trail from the village of Nenagh towards Dromineer and Lough Derg in County Tipperary. The walk starts on the northern side of the R445 Dublin Road to the east of the town. There's an information board here marking the starts of the walk which includes pictures of the wildlife you can see on the river. From here you head north along the pleasant riverside path. Continuing along the Slí Eala (Way of the Swan) trail, the path meanders through picturesque countryside, offering walkers a tranquil nature experience. The route is relatively flat, making it accessible for most fitness levels. As you approach Dromineer, the landscape opens up to the expansive views of Lough Derg, one of Ireland's largest lakes, providing a serene conclusion to the walk. The Nenagh River and its surrounding habitats support a diverse range of flora and fauna. Walkers may encounter mute swans gliding gracefully on the water, a species that has become emblematic of the trail. The riverbanks are adorned with various wildflowers, attracting pollinators such as butterflies and bees. Birdwatchers might also spot kingfishers, herons, and other waterfowl along the way. You can continue your walking around Nenagh on the Lough Derg Way or on the nearby climbs to Keeper Hill and the Millennium Cross Loop .
